marks.gloss_en: a blemish should disqualify the heifer of the broken neck too, a fortiori from the red heifer
'asher ein bah mum' -- in IT a blemish disqualifies, and no blemish disqualifies the heifer of the broken neck
the red heifer is disqualified by a blemish
the egla should import blemish-disqualification via 'ol'-'ol' from the para
הא מיעט רחמנא 'בה' -- the Merciful One excluded it: the same 'bah' forecloses the gezera-shava route as well
'ol' is stated of the para (Num 19:2) and 'ol' of the egla (Deut 21:3): as other labors disqualify there, they disqualify the para here
בעגלה נמי כתיב 'בה' -- the egla's own miut should block the import of its labor-law to the para
that 'bah' is required to exclude kodashim from labor-disqualification (against the kodashim KV), so it does not block the gezera shava
labor should disqualify sacred offerings, a fortiori from the heifer of the broken neck
'asher lo ubad bah' -- with IT labor disqualifies, and labor does not disqualify kodashim
the 'bah' of Deut 21:3 excludes sacred offerings: labor does not disqualify them
מה לעגלה שכן שנים פוסלות בה -- the source case carries a stringency kodashim lack
אטו קדשים מי ליכא דפסלי בהו שנים -- some offerings ARE disqualified by years; the verse is needed precisely for those, where the pircha has no grip
if the egla, which a blemish does not disqualify, other labors disqualify, then the para, which a blemish disqualifies -- is it not right that other labors disqualify it?
מיתיבי -- the baraita derives the para's labor-disqualification from the egla, and from the place you came: as the egla is disqualified only once it pulls, so the para (46a.14)
מה לעגלה שכן שנים פוסלות בה -- the egla carries the years-stringency the para lacks
קדשים יוכיחו -- kodashim, which a blemish disqualifies yet labor does not, prove the transfer invalid
'that upon which never CAME a yoke' -- read with the pause, the verse amplifies: disqualified in any case, whatever the labor
for the para: a yoke disqualifies even outside the time of labor; other labors disqualify only at the time of labor
ואימא: 'asher lo alah aleha' klal, 'ol' prat -- nothing in the generalisation but the detail: a yoke yes, anything else no
'asher' is an amplification (ribuya), taking the verse out of the klal-uprat form
'that has not been worked with' amplifies likewise for the egla: any labor disqualifies
labors other than the yoke disqualify the heifer of the broken neck (from the ribui 'asher lo ubad')
ואימא: 'asher lo ubad bah' klal, 'ol' prat -- a yoke yes, anything else no
'asher' is an amplification (ribuya)
תנאי היא -- one tanna derives it from the egla (the GS, importing the pulling condition), one from the para itself (the ribui); Rav follows the latter
(entertained) the 'bah' of 'that has not been worked with [bah]' (Deut 21:3) excludes the PARA: labors other than the yoke would not disqualify it
Rav: if one placed a bundle of sacks on the red heifer it is disqualified at once -- mere placement, no pulling needed
even labor done in prohibition (e.g. on Shabbat) does not disqualify offerings -- what the second source adds
even labor done while the animals were already sacred does not disqualify -- what the third source adds
R. Yochanan (to R. Abahu): the disqualifying pull is the measure of a full yoke
the measure of a yoke along its width is a tefach (what phrasing it as 'a yoke's width' adds)
R. Yochanan ben Shaul: let what made no fruit be broken where nothing makes fruit, to atone for one not allowed to make fruit
